blog.takeawaysText1: Waking up at the end of a complete 90-minute sleep cycle eliminates sleep inertia.
blog.takeawaysText2: Subtract multiples of 90 minutes from your wake-up time, then deduct 15 minutes of sleep onset latency.
blog.takeawaysText3: Anchor your wake-up time. Keep it consistent even on weekends to prevent circadian phase shifts.
blog.takeawaysText4: Set your bedroom temperature to 65°F (18.3°C) and reduce ambient light to 0 lux to secure deep sleep.
blog.prosConsTitle: Pros & Cons: Sleep Calculators vs. Wearable Trackers
blog.prosConsDesc: When optimizing your sleep cycles, should you rely on mathematical planning (Sleep Calculators) or active biological tracking (Wearables like Apple Watch, Oura Ring, or Whoop)? Here is a side-by-side scientific comparison:
blog.rowComfortWearable: Low EMF, potential skin irritation or sleep distraction
blog.rowPlanWearable: Poor (Only reports data after you wake up)
prosList: Provides actionable target bedtimes to prevent waking mid-deep-sleep
Requires no charging, hardware updates, or bluetooth connections
Helps cultivate a highly predictable circadian routine naturally
Avoids sleep-related anxiety caused by constantly checking scores
consList: Cannot track micro-arousals (awakenings) that you don't remember
Assumes a standard 90-minute sleep cycle length
Does not log heart rate variability (HRV) or oxygen desaturation
